line: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 c4 Nb6 f4 dxe5 fxe5 Nc6 Be3 Bf5 Nc3
teaches: Develop in the order that keeps an answer ready for the opponent's most annoying jump. A knight coming to the square beside your queenside pawns is only a problem while the rook behind them is still at home — bring the other pieces out in the sequence that leaves that rook one move from covering it, and the jump stops being a threat before it is played.
explains: The knight comes to c3, holding d5 and b5 and clearing the way for the rook to swing to the c-file if the enemy knight hops in. It is the developing move that answers a move that has not happened.
